seo.title: How a Job Goes — Cedar Mill Plumbing
seo.description: Six steps from first call to wrap-up: phone call, estimate visit, written quote, scheduled work, on-site execution, and warranty documentation.

header.heading: How a Job Goes.
header.lead: Same path most of the time — phone call or contact form, estimate visit if it's a bigger job, written quote, scheduled work, photos and invoice at completion. No diagnostic fees, no surprise add-ons, no high-pressure pitch.

timeline.title: First Call or Contact Form
timeline.lead: Call (503) 555-0149 or use the contact form. Tell me briefly what's going on, where the house is, and how soon you need someone out. I'll tell you straight whether it's a flat-rate service call we can book directly or a bigger job that needs an estimate visit first.
items: A few sentences on what's happening (slow drain, no hot water, leak, etc.)
Neighborhood or zip — confirms it's inside the service area
How urgent — same week, next week, just an estimate, or actively leaking now
Same / next business day reply on the form. Phone is faster

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: Either a service call on the calendar with a flat-rate quote, or an estimate visit booked at your convenience.

timeline.title: Estimate Visit (if needed)
timeline.lead: For bigger jobs — water heater swap, repipe, slab leak, tankless conversion — I come out, walk the scope with you, take a few measurements and photos, and ask about anything that affects the install (gas line size, panel capacity, access points). No diagnostic fee, no "the price doubles if you don't sign today."
items: Walk the job, measure, and photograph the scope
Confirm anything that affects the install (gas, panel, venting, access)
Discuss timing, what's included, what isn't, and any code/permit requirements
Honest yes/no on whether I'm the right plumber for the job

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: A written estimate in your email by end of business that day — usually faster — with a flat number and a clear scope description.

timeline.title: Written Quote & Scheduling
timeline.duration: Same day, then a few business days to schedule
timeline.lead: Once you sign off on the written estimate (a quick reply works — no portal logins), I put you on the schedule. Non-emergency work typically lands inside 3 to 5 business days. Bigger projects (full repipe, multi-day work) book a week or two out depending on the season.
items: Estimate signed off via email — no portal account required
Deposit collected for projects over $2,500 (typically 30%)
Scheduled date confirmed, with a window — "Tuesday morning" or similar
Reminder text the day before, with an arrival time

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: A confirmed date on the calendar with a written scope and a price you can hold me to.

timeline.title: On-Site Work
timeline.duration: From an hour to a few days, depending on scope
timeline.lead: Show up on time, in the work truck. Boots come off at the door, drop cloths down on flooring, walk the scope with you one more time before we start. Service calls usually wrap inside the same visit. Multi-day jobs (repipes, tankless conversions) get a daily check-in so you know what's happening and what's next.
items: Arrival inside the agreed window — text if running late
Worksite protected with drop cloths and shoe covers
Permit work coordinated with the city or county where required
Daily wrap-up on multi-day jobs so the house stays usable

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: Work done to the written scope, with any in-flight scope changes confirmed in writing before the price moves.

timeline.title: Photos, Invoice, Walkthrough
timeline.lead: Before drywall closes (on bigger jobs) and at the end of every visit, I photograph the work — joints, runs, fittings, before-and-after on visible repairs. Walkthrough with you so you can see what was done, and the written invoice and photo report land in your email same day. Inspections (where required) scheduled and signed off by me, not subbed out.
items: Photo report of every fitting, run, and repair
Written invoice with the same number as the estimate (or revised in writing earlier)
Walkthrough so you see what changed and how to operate any new fixtures
Permit inspection scheduled and attended where required

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: Documentation in your email — invoice, photos, warranty terms — kept on file for the duration of the warranty.

timeline.title: Warranty & Follow-Up
timeline.lead: If anything I installed fails inside the warranty window, I come back and fix it free. Manufacturer warranty pass-through on water heaters, fixtures, and valves — I file the claim if a covered part fails. Most jobs don't need a follow-up; for ones that do, the call goes to the same plumber, not a warranty department.
items: 1-year workmanship warranty on standard service work
5-year workmanship warranty on whole-house repipes
Manufacturer warranty pass-through (typically 6-12 yrs water heaters, 25 yrs PEX)
Warranty calls handled by Mike directly — same number, same response time

deliverable.title: What you'll get
deliverable.body: A plumber who picks up the phone next time something needs work — and remembers the house.

finalCta.heading: Sound like the kind of plumber you want?
finalCta.body: First step is short and free — phone call or contact form. I'll tell you straight whether it's a flat-rate service call, an estimate visit, or something I'd refer to a colleague who specializes.
